decision: Retain all 9 informative targets as uncertain and all other targets as unmentioned. No automatic report selection, label duplication or virtual study splitting. Raw source and gold unchanged.
findings: Two complete current reports explicitly label right then left. The report field and entire train.csv are byte-identical in the archived source and existing root-obtained current authenticated Kaggle copy; no recovery corruption found. Six series form one coherent single-side-tagged acquisition set: axial PD FS, coronal PD FS, sagittal T2, sagittal PD FS, coronal T1 and an additional T1 sequence. All twelve sampled Laterality values are literal RIGHT; ImageLaterality and FrameLaterality are blank. SeriesNumbers3 through8, AcquisitionNumber1, one hashed PatientID, six hashed frames of reference. The two t1_se_cor_384 descriptions do not define two matching acquisitions: SeriesNumber6 has sagittal IOP agreeing with the other sagittal sequences, while SeriesNumber8 has coronal IOP. This is a description-orientation discrepancy, not proof of a second knee. No repeated full acquisition sets or mixed side tags are present.
root_verification: Personally read full original source and independent technical assessment including every series record. Verified all bound file sizes/SHA, source identity, exact series/header counts, side fields and current twelve report masks. Previous source/header flags were disclosed, so this is not a blinded discovery.
limits: RIGHT is preserved literally rather than silently normalized to the DICOM R value, and is header evidence rather than anatomical confirmation. Six separate frame-of-reference hashes limit direct cross-series coordinate comparison. Only lexical endpoint samples have been inspected; they are not necessarily geometric extremes, and unsampled slices could differ. No full-file source digest or native anatomy verified in this follow-up.
No native image viewing or anatomical laterality confirmation for this case. Absence of a repeated-set candidate does not prove one knee.
